 De Zerbi: Bergvall, Maddison, Savio in contention for Ipswich, Tel, Tosin, Mudryk out
 Three back, three out for Tottenham vs. Ipswich Town.
 by Dustin George-Miller Nov 20, 2026, 4:32 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 24: Roberto De Zerbi, head coach of Tottenham Hotspur, looks on as he arrives prior to the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on October 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Danehouse Photography Ltd/Getty Images) Getty Images Tottenham Hotspur play their first match in two weeks since their loss away at Leeds due to the November international break, and there’s good news! Speaking in his press conference , Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi confirmed that a trio of recently injured players — Lucas Bergvall, James Maddison, and Savio — are in contention to play when Spurs host Ipswich at teatime Saturday.
 However, Mathys Tel, who was injured by Jayden Bogle in Spurs’ last match, is still not ready to return, nor is Tosin Adarabioyo or Mykhailo Mudryk. There were reports last week that Tel’s ankle injury was not as serious as first feared and that there are expectations he could return soon; tel was spotted in Spurs’ training video montages in the past few days. But he’s still not quite ready, according to RDZ.
 “Bergvall, Maddison, Savio are back. Tosin and Mathys, no. Tosin is already okay but it’s not the right moment to take any risk. With Mathys, we need another I think, two, three weeks. Mudryk is not ready yet.
 “[Maddison] worked very well from last Wednesday after Leeds. He worked very well every day and before Leeds, from Chelsea game to Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch and training ground. If you don’t work during the week, you risk injury and in any way you lose the normal physical condition you need to play in Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work, when they are fit to work, they have many chances to play and especially Maddison because he is a special player.”
 The injury to Mathys Tel and Savio’s recent return could create a dilemma for De Zerbi as he plans to slightly rotate the squad for this and upcoming matches. If Savio isn’t ready to start (and that would not be a surprise), De Zerbi could opt to move Omar Marmoush to left wing with Dominic Solanke up top, or he could surprise everyone by handing a first Premier League start to academy graduate and exciting young talent Luca Williams-Barnett. But we won’t know that until the lineups are released tomorrow. De Zerbi was asked about that possibility.
 “Maybe, maybe. We have to see. I have not decided yet the first XI but when I have to select the first XI, I don’t start from the age. I start from the condition, the physical condition, the mental condition, the quality of the player and then the experience, but maybe he can be available and a good solution. We’ll have to see.”
 A lot of focus was paid to Mudryk in this press conference which felt a little weird considering he’s on loan and has played all of five minutes this season. Mudryk was recently in the news after giving a Ukranian-language interview where he, among other things, said that his dream move (before he joined Chelsea) was to play for Arsenal, and also criticized 20 mph speed limits in the United Kingdom. Mudryk has been injured for much of the season thus far after picking up a hamstring injury in training, and while it was thought that he might return about now apparently he had a minor setback.
 De Zerbi was asked about the interview, Mudryk’s Arsenal fandom, and when he might see the pitch again.
 ”Yes, I can understand the fans’ [irritation with the Arsenal connection], but Mudryk is a good guy, he’s a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he’s playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.
 ”He wants to work on the training ground and I think he has no responsibility in this part. But now I think his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play. He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he’s working hard to recover and to play earlier.
 “The plan was to play Ipswich or Sunderland or any way to be available. And then he felt no pain but not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more and step by step we’re going to see the situation.”
 De Zerbi will not be on the touchline for the Ipswich match, as he will be serving a one match ban for yellow card accumulation so far this season. This seems to be a bit of a point of contention with De Zerbi, who claimed his first two yellows were “unfair” and the third yellow was for arguing about a phantom call on Pedro Porro vs. Leeds. De Zerbi will be confined to the stands at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but will be able to talk to and message his staff from his seat during the match, and can speak to his team before the match and at intermission.
 “I’m used to sometimes to stay on the stand but this time it’s not fair. Because their yellow card in Chelsea was not for my responsibility. And the yellow card in Leeds was another time unfair. Because I got the yellow card not for the Mathys situation but for the Pedro Porro situation. It was no fault but I have to accept. You have a big, big staff, maybe better than me. The players can play without me, without problems.”
 Tottenham’s match against Ipswich kicks off at 10 am ET / 3 pm GMT. It is not televised in the UK, but will be broadcast on USA Network in the United States and streamed on nbcsports.com.
